title: Ambient exchange counit, shift compatibility and full-subcategory restriction
statement:
Fix the standing separated finite-type scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] and any commutative condensed ring $R$. Let $p:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, $p':X'\to Y'$ form a commutative square; it need not be cartesian. On ordinary unbounded derived module-object categories write $P_u=Lu^*$, $G_u=Ru_*$ with canonical adjunctions and counits $\varepsilon_u$, and let $\theta:P_{p'}P_g\cong P_{g'}P_p$ be the canonical pullback comparison. Define the ambient map
$$B:P_gG_p\longrightarrow G_{p'}P_{g'}$$
by the unit of $P_{p'}\dashv G_{p'}$, then $G_{p'}\theta$, then $G_{p'}P_{g'}\varepsilon_p$. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X})$, in right-to-left functional notation its components satisfy
$$\varepsilon_{p',P_{g'}K}\circ P_{p'}(B_K)=P_{g'}(\varepsilon_{p,K})\circ\theta_{G_pK}.$$
The two ambient functors are exact and $B$ commutes with their canonical integer-shift comparisons, hence induces morphisms of distinguished triangles including the connecting square. If the four pullbacks and two pushforwards in this formula preserve chosen full triangulated subcategories, and the restricted adjunctions/composition maps are their restrictions, then the restricted $B$ is exactly the unit--square--counit map of [det-def-sfb-base-change-morphism-bc], with the same components. In particular this applies to $\Dbc$ whenever these preservation hypotheses hold.
